key_insight: Cycle-World reduces long-video drift by enforcing reverse-prediction cycle consistency, helping the model stay temporally stable over many generated steps. In simple terms, it teaches the video world model to “close the loop” so small mistakes do not snowball into major visual collapse.
problem_solved: The paper addresses error accumulation in autoregressive diffusion-based video world models, where tiny prediction errors compound over time and cause generative drift, structural breakdown, and degraded long-horizon video quality.
method: Introduces Cycle-World, a framework that adds reverse-prediction cycle consistency to long-term video generation.
Uses a cycle-based training objective so forward predictions can be checked and corrected through reverse reconstruction.
Aims to stabilize temporal dynamics and reduce long-range drift in autoregressive video synthesis.
impact: This matters for practitioners building video generation, simulation, and world-model systems because it improves stability over long horizons, which is essential for realistic and coherent outputs. It can help make long-video synthesis more reliable for creative tools, robotics simulation, and predictive modeling.
visual_elements: A loop diagram showing forward prediction and reverse prediction forming a consistency cycle
A timeline comparing standard autoregressive drift vs. Cycle-World stability over long horizons
A side-by-side frame sequence illustrating visual degradation without the method and coherence with it
An icon-based flowchart highlighting error accumulation, cycle correction, and stable output
paper_title: Cycle-World: Mitigating Error Accumulation in Long-term Video World Models via Reverse-Prediction Cycle Consistency
paper_authors: Zihan Su, Teng Hu, Jiangning Zhang, Ruiyan Wang, Ran Yi
